target_customer: Small and mid-size nonprofits, churches, foundations and HOAs that pay for spend management cards and financial tools
problem: Nonprofits lack cards and spend tools built for grants and compliance, and they struggle with personal credit checks, receipts and manual reporting.
business_model: Fintech spend management with card interchange and software fees
product_category: Nonprofit spend management and financial management

founders.name: Matt Tengtrakool
education: Harvard, computer science and statistics, dropped out
previous_startups: A startup helping loan takers in Nigeria (unnamed on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Led two national nonprofits and served on national boards, per the YC page. TechCrunch in Dec 2025 calls him a 21-year-old dropout.

founders.name: Aidan Sunbury
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch and CB Insights, not on the YC page.

investors: angels including the CEOs of Chariot and Wealthfront

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing runs through bank and fintech partners (First Internet Bank, CapitalOS), so the hard parts are compliance, receipt matching and accounting sync rather than core banking.

defensibility.rationale: Corporate spend platforms can serve nonprofits with similar features, and the card issuer is a partner. Accounting sync and grant budgeting create some switching cost once a nonprofit adopts it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in Dec 2025 says features resemble Ramp and Brex and that Givefront layers on top of legacy nonprofit accounting. Another nonprofit finance startup, Crowded, raised a 7.5M Series A in early 2025. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: Nonprofits often cannot get cards without personal guarantees and rely on spreadsheets. Demand evidence is the company's traction claims: hundreds of organizations onboarded within about six months of card launch and over 200 percent monthly growth, per TechCrunch in Dec 2025.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission led with the tagline The easiest way to save money for your nonprofit

branding.community_and_virality: A CBS Austin and KUTV segment covered a young entrepreneur building the first credit card for nonprofits, per search results, not opened.

brand_strength.rationale: A name that signals the nonprofit giving niche and is easy to say, with some local TV and TechCrunch coverage. CB Insights lists the company as formerly Clav, but no source gives the date or reason.

outcome_analysis: Givefront went through YC Winter 2024 as a six-person team and raised a 2 million dollar seed led by Script Capital in December 2025 after launching cards. Company stated traction of hundreds of organizations and fast monthly growth suggests early fit in a niche that larger spend platforms underserve. Risks are interchange margin dependence and Ramp or Brex moving down market.
notes: Seed cross-checked by TechCrunch, Pulse and CB Insights, which also lists total funding of 2.5M. A roughly 500K pre-seed or angel round in Feb 2024 appears only in trackers and is unverified so not recorded as a round. Rename from Clav is per CB Insights only. Competitors Ramp and Brex come from a Dec 2025 article, not near the batch, so the list is empty. Traction claims are company statements.
